The D Flip-Flop is a synchronous device.
		When HIGH input is applied to the D input, the state of the flip-flop is set to HIGH.
		When LOW input is applied to the D input, the state of the flip-flop is set to LOW.
		However the state of the flip-flop will be flashed to the output Q and Q' only when the clock signal changes its state. Changing the D input while the clock signal is HIGH or LOW will not affect the output of the flip-flop. The set state of the flip-flop is flashed to the output only when a transition of the clock signal has occurred.

\t\tThe D latch outputs the D input whenever the Enable line is HIGH, otherwise the output is whatever the D input was when the Enable input was last HIGH. This is why it is also known as a transparent latch - when Enable is asserted, the latch is said to be \"transparent\" - signals propagate directly through it as if it isn\'t there. D latches can be used as 1-bit memory circuits, storing either a HIGH or a LOW state when disabled, and \"reading\" new data from the D input when enabled.

\t\tThe data distributor, known more commonly as a Demultiplexer or “Demux” for short, is the exact opposite of the Multiplexer. A demultiplexer is a combinational circuit that has one data information input d and n control inputs that are used to select one of the 2^n outputs, through which the data present at the input must be output.\n\t\tThis is achieved by applying to the control inputs the binary combination corresponding to the output to be selected. The demultiplexer takes one single input data line and then switches it to any one of a number of individual output lines one at a time.

\t\tA flip-flop is a device very much like a latch in that it is a bistable multivibrator, having two states and a feedback path that allows it to store a bit of information. The difference between a latch and a flip-flop is that a latch is asynchronous, and the outputs can change as soon as the inputs do (or at least after a small propagation delay). A flip-flop, on the other hand, is edge-triggered and only changes state when a control signal goes from HIGH to LOW or LOW to HIGH.

\t\tIn order to embed a circuit the IO nodes of the circuit you want to import must be set up. This can be done by opening the setup panel from the top toolbar - click Setup. \n\t\tFrom there any number of nodes can be added, so when the circuit is embedded in another one they can be used as connections. The IO pins can be arranged, renamed and their positions can be set (LEFT, TOP, RIGHT, BOTTOM).

The JK Flip-Flop is a synchronous device.
		When HIGH input is applied to the J input, the state of the flip-flop is set to HIGH.
		When HIGH input is applied to the K input, the state of the flip-flop is set to LOW.
		When HIGH input is applied to both J and K inputs, the state of the flip-flop is toggled.
		However the state of the flip-flop will be flashed to the output Q and Q' only when the clock signal changes its state. Changing J and K inputs while the clock signal is HIGH or LOW will not affect the output of the flip-flop. The set state of the flip-flop is flashed to the output only when a transition of the clock signal has occurred.

\t\tThe JK latch is an asynchronous device - it works independently of control signals and relies only on the state of the J and K inputs.\n\t\tWhen a HIGH input is applied to the J line of an JK latch, the Q output goes HIGH (and Q\' LOW). The feedback mechanism, however, means that the Q output will remain HIGH, even when the J input goes LOW again. This is how the latch serves as a memory device. Conversely, a HIGH input on the K line will drive the Q output LOW (and Q\' HIGH), effectively resetting the latch\'s \"memory\". When both inputs are LOW, the latch \"latches\" – it remains in its previously set or reset state. When both inputs are HIGH at once, the output will be toggled. The JK Latch works like SR Latch with the illegal state of both S and R set to HIGH, removed and made to toggle the output.

\t\tA latch is an example of a bistable multivibrator, that is, a device with exactly two stable states. These states are HIGH-output and LOW-output. A latch has a feedback path, so information can be retained by the device. Therefore latches can be memory devices, and can store one bit of data. As the name suggests, latches are used to \"latch onto\" information and hold in place. Latches are very similar to flip-flops, but are not synchronous devices, and do not operate on clock edges as flip-flops do.

\t\tA segment display is a form of electronic display device for displaying decimal numerals that is an alternative to the more complex dot matrix displays. Segment displays are widely used in digital clocks, electronic meters, basic calculators, and other electronic devices that display numerical information.\n\t\tSegment displays may use a liquid crystal display (LCD), a light-emitting diode (LED) for each segment, an electrochromic display, or other light-generating or controlling techniques such as cold cathode gas discharge (Panaplex), vacuum fluorescent (VFD), incandescent filaments (Numitron), and others. For gasoline price totems and other large signs, vane displays made up of electromagnetically flipped light-reflecting segments (or \"vanes\") are still commonly used. An alternative to the 7-segment display in the 1950s through the 1970s was the cold-cathode, neon-lamp-like nixie tube.

\t\tThe AND gate is a digital logic gate that implements logical conjunction. The output state of a digital logic AND gate only returns HIGH when ALL of its inputs are at a logic level HIGH. In other words for a logic AND gate, any LOW input will give a LOW output. The Boolean expression for AND gate is that for Logical Multiplication: A.B.C = Q.

\t\tA simple 3-input logic AND gate can be constructed using transistors connected together with the inputs connected directly to the transistor bases. All transistors must be saturated ON for an output at Q.

\t\tThe AND gate is a digital logic gate that implements logical conjunction. The output state of a digital logic AND gate only returns HIGH when ALL of its inputs are at a logic level HIGH. In other words for a logic AND gate, any LOW input will give a LOW output. The Boolean expression for AND gate is that for Logical Multiplication: A.B = Q.

\t\tA simple 2-input logic AND gate can be constructed using transistors connected together with the inputs connected directly to the transistor bases. Both transistors must be saturated “ON” for an output at Q.
\t\tA BCD to Seven Segment decoder is a combinational logic circuit that accepts a decimal digit in BCD (input) and generates appropriate outputs for the segments to display the input decimal digit.

\t\tA BUFFER has only a single input and a single output. It simply passes its input, unchanged, to its output. BUFFER is mainly used to increase propagation delay. In a real-world circuit, a buffer can be used to amplify a signal if its current is too weak.
\t\tTwo inverters(NOT gates) connected in series so as to invert, then re-invert the signal, functioning as a buffer.
\t\tButtons can be used to output a logic level HIGH or LOW, according to its state. The state of a button is HIGH when its pressed and LOW when its not.
\t\tSignal generators have one output. This output is set to level HIGH for half of the cycle and then back to LOW at intervals which are defined by the frequency of the generator.
\t\tThese elements have only one output. They provide HIGH state on their output. This state is not changed over time. Their output can be connected to many nodes.

\t\tAn integrated circuit or monolithic integrated circuit (also referred to as an IC, a chip, or a microchip) is a set of electronic circuits on one small flat piece (or \"chip\") of semiconductor material that is normally silicon. The integration of large numbers of tiny MOS transistors into a small chip results in circuits that are orders of magnitude smaller, faster, and less expensive than those constructed of discrete electronic components. ICs are now used in virtually all electronic equipment and have revolutionized the world of electronics. Computers, mobile phones, and other digital home appliances are now inextricable parts of the structure of modern societies, made possible by the small size and low cost of ICs.\n\t\tIn this application you can add whole projects as an IC. This helps with modularity of your projects.
\t\tLights can be used to indicate the level of the input signal. When the input is at HIGH level the light glow and when the input is at LOW level it doesn\'t glow.
\t\tThese elements have only one output. They provide LOW state on their output. This state is not changed over time. Their output can be connected to many nodes.

\t\tThe NAND (Not – AND) gate has an output that is at logic level HIGH and only goes to logic level LOW when ALL of its inputs are at logic level HIGH. The Logic NAND Gate is the reverse or Complementary form of the AND gate.

\t\tA simple 3-input logic AND gate can be constructed using transistors connected together with the inputs connected directly to the transistor bases. Either transistor must be cut-off OFF for an output at Q.

\t\tThe NAND (Not – AND) gate has an output that is at logic level HIGH and only goes to logic level LOW when ALL of its inputs are at logic level HIGH. The Logic NAND Gate is the reverse or Complementary form of the AND gate.

\t\tA simple 2-input logic NAND gate can be constructed using transistors connected together with the inputs connected directly to the transistor bases. Either transistor must be cut-off OFF for an output at Q.

\t\tThe inclusive NOR (Not-OR) gate has an output that is at logic level HIGH and only goes LOW when ANY of its inputs are at logic level HIGH. The Logic NOR Gate is the reverse or Complementary form of OR gate.

\t\tA simple 3-input logic NOR gate can be constructed using transistors connected together with the inputs connected directly to the transistor bases. All transistors must be cut-off OFF for an output at Q.

\t\tThe inclusive NOR (Not-OR) gate has an output that is at logic level HIGH and only goes LOW when ANY of its inputs are at logic level HIGH. The Logic NOR Gate is the reverse or Complementary form of OR gate.

\t\tA simple 2-input logic NOR gate can be constructed using transistors connected together with the inputs connected directly to the transistor bases. Both transistors must be cut-off OFF for an output at Q.
\t\tInverting NOT gates have an output level that is normally at logic level HIGH and goes LOW when its single input is at logic level HIGH, in other words it inverts (complements) its input signal.
\t\tA simple logic NOT gate can be constructed using a transistor with the input connected directly to the transistor base. The transistor must be saturated ON for an inverted output OFF at Q.

\t\tThe OR gate is a digital logic gate that implements logical disjunction. The output state of a digital logic OR gate returns HIGH when ANY of its inputs are at a logic level HIGH. In other words for a logic OR gate, only if ALL inputs are LOW will give a LOW output. The Boolean expression for OR gate is that for Logical Addition: A+B+C = Q.

\t\tA simple 3-input logic OR gate can be constructed using transistors connected together with the inputs connected directly to the transistor bases. Either transistor must be saturated ON for an output at Q.

\t\tThe OR gate is a digital logic gate that implements logical disjunction. The output state of a digital logic OR gate returns HIGH when ANY of its inputs are at a logic level HIGH. In other words for a logic OR gate, only if ALL inputs are LOW will give a LOW output. The Boolean expression for OR gate is that for Logical Addition: A+B = Q.

\t\tA simple 2-input logic OR gate can be constructed using transistors connected together with the inputs connected directly to the transistor bases. Either transistor must be saturated ON for an output at Q.

\t\tA light-emitting diode (LED) is a semiconductor light source that emits light when current flows through it. Electrons in the semiconductor recombine with electron holes, releasing energy in the form of photons. The color of the light (corresponding to the energy of the photons) is determined by the energy required for electrons to cross the band gap of the semiconductor. White light is obtained by using multiple semiconductors or a layer of light-emitting phosphor on the semiconductor device. LEDs have many advantages over incandescent light sources, including lower energy consumption, longer lifetime, improved physical robustness, smaller size, and faster switching. LEDs are used in applications as diverse as aviation lighting, automotive headlamps, advertising, general lighting, traffic signals, camera flashes, lighted wallpaper, horticultural grow lights, and medical devices.

\t\tA Dot-Matrix Display is a display device which contains light emitting diodes aligned in the form of matrix. This Dot matrix displays are used in applications where Symbol, Graphic, Characters, Alphabets, Numerals are need to be displayed together in static as well as Scrolling motion.Dot Matrix Display is manufactured in various dimensions like 5x7,8x8,16x8,128x16, 128x32 and 128x64 where the numbers represent LED\'s in rows and columns, respectively. Also these displays comes in different colors such as Red, Green, Yellow, Blue, Orange, White.
\t\tSwitches can be used to output a logic level HIGH or LOW, according to its state. Toggle it to set its output state to HIGH. Toggle it again to set its output state to LOW.

\t\tThe output state of a digital logic XNOR gate returns HIGH when the inputs are on SAME levels. In other words for a logic XNOR gate, DIFFERENT input levels (no matter HIGH or LOW) will give a LOW output. Ex-NOR gates are used mainly in electronic circuits that perform arithmetic operations and data checking such as Adders, Subtractors or Parity Checkers, etc.
\t\tAn XNOR gate circuit can be made from five NAND gates or mixed.

\t\tThe XOR gate is a digital logic gate that implements logical exclusive disjunction. The output state of a digital logic XOR gate returns HIGH when the inputs are on DIFFERENT levels. In other words for a logic XOR gate, SAME input levels (no matter HIGH or LOW) will give a LOW output. The Boolean expression for XOR gate is: A⊕B = Q.
\t\tAn XOR gate circuit can be made from four NAND gates, five NOR gates and mixed.

\t\tMultiplexing is the generic term used to describe the operation of sending one or more digital signals over a common line and as such, the device we use to do just that is called a Multiplexer. The multiplexer is a combinational logic circuit designed to switch one of several input lines to a single common output line by the application of a control signal. This is achieved by applying to the control inputs the binary combination corresponding to the output to be selected.

\t\tA programmable array logic (PAL) is a kind of programmable logic device used to implement combinational logic circuits. The PAL has a set of programmable AND gate planes, which link to a set of fixed OR gate planes, which can then be conditionally complemented to produce an output. \n\t\tPALs differ from Programmable Logic Array devices (PLAs) in that only the AND gate plane is programmable. PAL is used for implementation of various combinational circuits using buffer, AND gate and OR gate. Programmable-AND and fixed-OR structure of PALs make them less flexible from programming point of view when compared with Programmable Logic Arrays (PLAs). However due to the same reason PALs are less expensive than PLAs.

\t\tA programmable logic array (PLA) is a kind of programmable logic device used to implement combinational logic circuits. The PLA has a set of programmable AND gate planes, which link to a set of programmable OR gate planes, which can then be conditionally complemented to produce an output.\n\t\tPLAs differ from Programmable Array Logic devices (PALs) in that both the AND and OR gate planes are programmable. PLA is used for implementation of various combinational circuits using buffer, AND gate and OR gate. In PLA, all the minterms are not realized but only required minterms are implemented. As PLA has programmable AND gate array and programmable OR gate array, it provides more flexibility but disadvantage is, it is not easy to use.

\t\tRead Only Memory ROM is a memory device, which stores the binary information permanently. That means, we can\'t change that stored information by any means later. If the ROM has programmable feature, then it is called as Programmable ROM PROM. The user has the flexibility to program the binary information electrically once by using PROM programmer. \n\t\tPROM is a programmable logic device that has fixed AND array and Programmable OR array. Here, the inputs of AND gates are not of programmable type. So, we have to generate 2^n product terms by using 2^n AND gates having n inputs each. We can implement these product terms by using nx2^n decoder. So, this decoder generates \'n\' min terms.

The SR Flip-Flop (Set/Reset) is a synchronous device.
		When HIGH input is applied to the S input, the state of the flip-flop is set to HIGH.
		When HIGH input is applied to the R input, the state of the flip-flop is set to LOW.
		However the state of the flip-flop will be flashed to the output Q and Q' only when the clock signal changes its state. HIGH state for both S and R inputs is illegal as it causes LOW state on both Q and Q' outputs. Changing S and R inputs while the clock signal is HIGH or LOW will not affect the output of the flip-flop. The set state of the flip-flop is flashed to the output only when a transition of the clock signal has occurred.

\t\tIn some situations it may be desirable to dictate when the latch can and cannot latch. The gated SR latch is a simple extension of the SR latch which provides an Enable line which must be driven HIGH before data can be latched. When the Enable input is LOW, the outputs remain latched to the previous data.

\t\tThe SR latch (Set/Reset) is an asynchronous device - it works independently of control signals and relies only on the state of the S and R inputs.\n\t\tWhen a HIGH input is applied to the Set line of an SR latch, the Q output goes HIGH (and Q\' LOW). The feedback mechanism, however, means that the Q output will remain HIGH, even when the S input goes LOW again. This is how the latch serves as a memory device. Conversely, a HIGH input on the Reset line will drive the Q output LOW (and Q\' HIGH), effectively resetting the latch\'s \"memory\". When both inputs are LOW, the latch \"latches\" – it remains in its previously set or reset state. When both inputs are HIGH at once, however, there is a problem: it is being told to simultaneously produce a LOW Q and a LOW Q\'. This produces an \"invalid condition\" within the circuit.
Starting a new record for this timing diagram will erase any previous data.

\t\tThe T Flip-Flop is a synchronous device.\n\t\tWhen HIGH input is applied to the T input, the state of the flip-flop is toggled.\n\t\tHowever the state of the flip-flop will be flashed to the output Q and Q\' only when the clock signal changes its state. Changing the T input while the clock signal is HIGH or LOW will not affect the output of the flip-flop. The set state of the flip-flop is flashed to the output only when a transition of the clock signal has occurred.

\t\tThe T latch toggles the output when T has become to HIGH state while the enable signal is at HIGH or the enable signal has become to HIGH state while the T input is at HIGH state. The function of the T Latch is just to toggle the output. It works as a JK Latch with its J and K inputs shorted.

\t\tDelays are often used for testing. Here the delay can be adjusted from 100ms to 120s. Timers are often implemented by 555 Timer. The 555 Timer gets its name from the fact that there are three internally connected 5kΩ resistors which it uses to generate the two comparators reference voltages. \n\t\t This IC can be used to produce variety of applications: one-shot delay timers, pulse generation, alarms, tone variations, clocks. The single 555 Timer chip in its basic form is a Bipolar 8-pin device.

\t\tOff Timers are with default output state of LOW. When a pulse is triggered to the \"Trigger\" input the output state is changed to HIGH immediately, then after the specified delay the output is set back to LOW.
\t\tOn Timers are with default output state of LOW. When a pulse is triggered to the \"Trigger\" input the output state is changed to HIGH after the specified delay.

\t\tWhen creating timing diagrams in circuits which include frequency generators keep in mind that the recording will not run in real time, but much slower. \n\t\tOne clock of the generator will be mapped to 3 seconds (realtime) and the elements latency will be kept at 16ms (realtime).

\t\tAs well as the standard Digital Buffer, there is another type of digital buffer circuit whose output can be “electronically” disconnected from its output circuitry when required. This type of Buffer is known as a 3-State Buffer or more commonly a Tri-state Buffer.\n\t\tA Tri-state Buffer can be thought of as an input controlled switch with an output that can be electronically turned “ON” or “OFF” by means of an external “Control” or “Enable” ( EN ) signal input. This control signal can be either a logic “0” or a logic “1” type signal resulting in the Tri-state Buffer being in one state allowing its output to operate normally producing the required output or in another state were its output is blocked or disconnected.\n\t\tWhen Enable signal is LOW the state of the tri-state buffer is neither at a logic “HIGH” or “LOW”, but instead gives an output state of very high impedance - High-Z. Then this type of device has two logic state inputs, “0” or a “1” but can produce three different output states, “0”, “1” or ” High-Z ” which is why it is called a “Tri” or “3-state” device.
\t\tStart creating project by clicking the red button in the bottom end corner. This button leads to the circuit screen where it can be implemented.

\t\tThis is the circuit editing screen. The top toolbar gives basic tools to work with the circuit. Cut, Copy, Paste commands. Undo redo and changing selection modes. To add elements click the button in the bottom end corner. A bottom sheet with the available elements will pop up.

\t\tAdding elements is easy - in one click. Clicking over an element will add the element to the circuit. Many elements can be added by clicking over them, when finished, the same button can be clicked to close the bottom sheet or just swiping it down.
